newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's Macondray seeks approval for float.
newsitem.headline: Manila's Macondray seeks approval for float.

text.p: Holding firm Macondray and Company Inc (MCI) said on Tuesday it had sought the approval of the Philippine Stock Exchange for an initial public offering.

It plans to offer 83 million to 191 million shares at a proposed offer price ranging from 13.08 pesos to 22.44 pesos, equivalent to 11.5 times to 18 times 1997 earnings, the company said in a statement.
A company spokeswoman told Reuters MCI plans to issue the shares in 1997. Its underwriters are Asian Alliance Investment Corp for the domestic tranche and ING Barings for its overseas sales.
The proceeds of the float will be used to repay debt related to its expansion and 600 million pesos will be set aside as advances to subsidiaries, the spokeswoman said.
MCI has previously said it expects net income of 620 million pesos this year, an increase of about 250 percent from 1996.
The company made a net income of 175 million pesos in 1996, a 63 percent jump from 107 million pesos in 1995.
Its consolidated revenues in 1996 amounted to 5.8 billion pesos, a 314 percent increase from 1.4 billion pesos in 1995.
The company has investments in food, consumer finance, packaging and distribution.
